Workload phase vectors may summarize execution, while specification links, timing constraints, power-domain descriptions, and authorized library corners retain the conditions those vectors do not express.

An action $a$, such as changing a compiler schedule or cache capacity, proposes a successor state $s'$. In our mapping study, a schedule edit changes the executed memory-access stream, so the successor cannot silently inherit the old schedule's trace. The state must identify which observations remain applicable, which become stale, and which are still missing. As several proposed edits accumulate, their predictions can also move beyond the model's training support. The representation keeps those proposals inspectable through three properties:

- **Design ancestry and constraints:** Intermediate states $s'$ identify their parent design and the requirements that still apply.
- **Evaluation sources and fidelity:** State representations link analytical bounds, cycle-level traces, and implementation returns without treating them as interchangeable observations. A predicted successor needs a constructible candidate and the relevant checks before it can be treated as an evaluated design.
- **Constructible outputs:** Changes proposed in a learned space must map back to explicit compiler inputs or hardware artifacts. Syntax, typing, functional, and physical checks establish which requirements the resulting candidate satisfies.

An agent can use this state to retrieve an applicable design note, request a new measurement when a dependency changes, and retain a checked result for later work. Storing a predicted successor does not make it an executed candidate. A proposed floorplan, for example, must return to the native placement database and pass legalization before its coordinates describe a legal layout.[^fn-eda-legalization-c04] If the state omits an electrical relationship entirely, checks that read only syntax can miss a serious physical defect, as the level-shifter example illustrates.

[^fn-eda-legalization-c04]: **Placement legalization**: In EDA, global placement algorithms position standard cells and macros continuously, often producing cell overlaps and off-grid positions. Legalization snaps cells into discrete, non-overlapping rows and power rails without violating minimum spacing design rules. In learned floorplanning, continuous coordinates that look good before legalization can lose routability or timing once cells are snapped into rows, an analogous gap between a continuous proposal and a legal design.

::: {.callout-failure-mode title="The missing level shifter"}
**The trap.** A text-based HDL netlist connecting a low-voltage core domain to higher-voltage I/O pads can pass structural syntax checks despite being electrically unsound.

**The mechanism.** When the selected cells require level shifting, missing power-domain information can leave the crossing without the required interface circuitry, so a low-voltage signal may fail to drive a higher-voltage receiver to a valid logic level or leave transistors partially conducting while other incompatible voltage crossings stress devices. Although the exact electrical consequences depend on the cells and operating conditions (and this scenario is a constructed failure example rather than a documented incident on a named processor), Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) 1801 UPF supplies an explicit representation for power intent that the tool flow can use and check.

**The lesson.** Textual HDL syntax checks must be supplemented with explicit multi-domain representations. Representations must carry power-domain relationships and voltage-crossing contracts in mechanically verifiable forms so that the relevant checks can detect illegal crossings before fabrication.
:::

## Data Licensing, Privacy, and Provenance {#sec-architecture-data-access}

A representation can capture every required electrical and physical domain and still remain legally or operationally restricted. Production architecture relies on foundry process design kits (PDKs, such as TSMC N7 or N3 kits) and proprietary IP blocks governed by nondisclosure agreements (NDAs). Substituting an open cell library for that restricted collateral changes the technical question along with the access terms, because a surrogate calibrated on an educational library such as Nangate45 cannot predict a 3\ nm implementation, where transistor behavior, wire parasitics,[^fn-wire-parasitics-c04] and cell footprints diverge sharply. A dataset therefore has to record both its technical conditions and its legal boundaries, including PDK revisions, NDA scopes, tool license terms, and permitted recipients, so that an architect never mistakes an accessible academic proxy for evidence about a production process.

[^fn-wire-parasitics-c04]: **Wire parasitics**: The distributed resistance ($R$) and capacitance ($C$) associated with physical on-chip interconnects. As process nodes shrink from 45\ nm to 3\ nm, wire resistance per unit length rises steeply because cross-sections narrow and electron scattering at surfaces and grain boundaries increases, so interconnect delay increasingly dominates on long wires.

Even when a team holds legitimate access to production collateral, the governing agreements rarely grant a blanket right to use those files in machine learning workflows. Training, retrieval, transformation, and redistribution carry distinct legal boundaries across foundry PDKs, commercial interconnect IP (such as PCIe or DDR controllers), Liberty (`.lib`) timing files, and Library Exchange Format (LEF) physical layouts.[^fn-physical-formats-c04] Permission to integrate an IP block into an internal chip does not establish permission to send it to an external large language model endpoint or incorporate it into a public training corpus [@LongpreEtAl2024DataProvenance]; instead, proprietary netlist fragments, SPICE decks, and place-and-route reports usually require running models inside environments that the governing agreements permit, often on premises. Auditing whether generated RTL reproduces proprietary collateral therefore requires logging the provenance of retrieved context and running similarity checks inside that secure boundary without exposing the protected IP.

[^fn-physical-formats-c04]: **Physical design collateral (`.lib` and LEF)**: Liberty (`.lib`) timing libraries supply characterized cell propagation delays, setup-and-hold tables, and leakage values across operating corners. LEF files provide abstract cell boundaries, pin geometries, and metal routing obstructions required for macro placement and routing.

These legal boundaries also limit what an outside reviewer can reproduce. While public benchmarks built on open PDKs (such as SkyWater 130\ nm or IHP 130\ nm) allow researchers to compare methods under open conditions, claims about commercial production nodes still depend on private foundry verification. Teams can bridge this gap by adapting *Datasheets for Datasets* to computer architecture [@GebruEtAl2021Datasheets], publishing permitted schemas, collection procedures, toolchain manifests, artifact hashes, and evaluation policies so that independent reviewers can audit the structure of a study while proprietary silicon collateral remains secured in approved environments. Inside the active workflow, those same schemas, provenance links, and access limits must be packaged into an explicit handoff so that downstream design methods know what they are allowed to change and how their proposals will be checked.

## Handing a Represented Problem to a Method

A method needs to know which information it can use now, which changes it can express, and which observations it must obtain before comparing candidates. Those answers connect the dataset to the live design state. They also prevent a retrieved design note from passing as a current constraint or a planned simulation from appearing as an available training example.

The prospective Lighthouse mapping study makes the distinction concrete. Its workload and target descriptions define the intended comparison, but no timing dataset or working compiler backend has yet been built. The representation can specify operator shapes, candidate schedules, required numerical behavior, and the observations to collect without claiming that those observations already exist. A future agent could consult an applicable scheduling example, propose a constructible schedule, and request its evaluation; each step uses a different part of the represented information.

::: {.callout-design-principle title="Represent what the decision must preserve"}
**The principle:** A representation that cannot express a constraint the decision depends on cannot be checked against it, so every such constraint must be explicit in the representation or linked to the source and check that establish it.

**The application:** Expose the functional and physical relationships a decision relies on, or link directly to the sources and checks needed to establish them.
:::

### Expressible Changes and Their Dependencies

A tile-size vector permits changes within a schedule template. A dependency graph can support changes to operation ordering or fusion, provided the compiler has transformations that preserve the required computation. This distinguishes *parametric changes*, which select values within a prescribed template, from *structural changes*, which alter components or their relationships. The boundary depends on the generator: alternative pipeline depths or topologies can themselves be parameters if the generator already supports them.

Even a parameter change has dependencies beyond its scalar value. Changing cache capacity can require a new SRAM bank organization, wrapper instantiation, and matching hierarchical paths in timing and power constraints. An encoding that exposes only capacity hides the work needed to construct the candidate. Likewise, a schedule edit changes generated code and can invalidate the trace used to estimate memory traffic or switching activity. These dependency links tell the system which observations to refresh after an action.

Numerical encoding addresses a different question. A linear capacity feature emphasizes absolute differences, while a logarithmic feature emphasizes relative changes [@LeeBrooks2006RegressionModeling]. Neither establishes whether a proposed capacity can be built. A schema indexed by supported SRAM organizations can restrict proposals to available implementations, while a method that proposes a new organization needs a path to the tools that will construct and check it. Representation therefore determines both how candidates are compared computationally and which candidates can reach evaluation.

### Available Information and Missing Observations

The mapping study varies software while holding the accelerator target fixed. The cache study introduced in @sec-architecture-20-ontology varies hardware while holding the compiled software fixed. Their handoffs need the same kinds of information, but their dependencies and acquisition costs differ (@tbl-represented-problem).

| **Handoff field** | **Prospective mapping study** | **Prospective cache study** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Expressible change** | Tile sizes and schedules, or supported compiler transformations. | Capacity choices that resolve to realizable cache organizations. |
| **Information available before execution** | Workload descriptions, operator shapes, schedule structure, target parameters, and numerical requirements. | Fixed software and workload identities, candidate capacities, and supported SRAM organizations. |
| **Observations to acquire** | Correctness results, execution latency, memory transfers, and stalls for candidate schedules. | Matched frame-time observations and SRAM power, area, and access-time estimates. |
| **Dependencies to refresh** | Generated binaries and traces when the schedule changes. | Cache instances and dependent constraints when capacity or bank organization changes. |
| **Collection cost to expose** | Backend preparation, compilation, correctness checks, and execution across shapes and schedules. | The bounded cycle-level and SRAM evaluations specified by the study, including reruns and diagnosis. |
| **Missing information to retain** | The timing dataset and working backend are not yet available; kernel observations alone will not establish full-frame behavior. | Execution history is initially empty; layout congestion, thermal behavior, and IR drop remain outside the screening observations. |
: **A representation handoff distinguishes usable inputs from observations still to be acquired.** These prospective studies share a reusable set of fields while varying different parts of the hardware–software system. {#tbl-represented-problem tbl-colwidths="[22,39,39]"}

The dependency row explains why the two studies cannot share a collection policy blindly. A new software schedule changes the access stream, so the mapping study must capture the candidate's behavior. A cache comparison holds the binary fixed, but still needs a model that captures the timing feedback relevant to its question. In both cases, a missing measurement remains explicit even when a cheap estimate is available.

The handoff can point into existing specifications, experiment databases, and versioned artifacts rather than duplicate them in a new document. It must make their current applicability, permitted use, and unresolved gaps accessible to the method. With that information, a downstream design system can distinguish using an existing observation from acquiring a new one, and proposing a candidate from establishing its behavior.

## Open Questions

Building source-linked datasets and machine-usable representations for an architectural study exposes five open research problems across dataset curation, benchmark splitting, representation design, cross-layer provenance, and workload modeling:

- **How should we train models and collect data when many tool runs crash, time out, or fail physical checks?** Public physical-design datasets such as CircuitNet discard runs that fail placement or routing [@ChaiEtAl2022CircuitNet], yet training surrogates only on the layouts that survive omits observations near the physical feasibility boundary. Different failures carry different lessons: a missed target-frequency check gives a left-censored bound on sustainable clock rate, whereas an EDA router timeout leaves circuit delay unresolved, and dense fanout or pin crowding can make those missing results depend on the candidate. Survival-aware training can use qualified censored bounds, while unresolved physical outcomes require separate treatment. Under tight tool-license budgets, we still need training objectives and active data-collection policies that preserve these distinctions when deciding whether to diagnose an aborted run, sample nearby legal configurations, or record a supported feasibility boundary.

- **How do we split hardware datasets into training and test sets when parameterized generators share circuit structure across configurations?** A row split can test unseen configurations within a familiar Chisel, FIRRTL, or SystemVerilog `generate` template. If the claim concerns new design families, however, shared templates across training and test sets can make familiar circuit structure look like evidence of cross-family transfer. Protein engineering and molecular machine learning faced this same leakage problem and replaced random row splits with sequence-identity cutoffs and shared chemical core partitions, but hardware still lacks an agreed distance metric, and putting every design from a parameterized generator into one split can starve the training set of structural variety. Dataset builders need quantitative structural-similarity metrics over elaborated netlists and syntax trees so that benchmark splits match the actual generalization claim, from interpolating queue depths inside a known template to extrapolating across new interconnect topologies.

- **How can a hardware representation prevent electrically or protocol-illegal designs by construction without ruling out unconventional topologies?** A flat stream of text tokens permits edits that drop flow-control backpressure signals or omit voltage level shifters across power domains, leaving downstream simulation and implementation tools to find the defects. Restricting a method to checked configurations within a fixed template can prevent some malformed proposals, but excludes structural changes the template cannot express. The challenge is to expose more legal changes while preserving the invariants that static checks can establish and identifying which protocol and electrical properties still need deeper verification.

- **How can compilers and synthesis tools trace a physical timing or routing failure back to the high-level design choice that caused it?** As a computation is lowered from high-level MLIR tensor dialects (`linalg` and `affine`) through CIRCT structural dialects (`comb` and `seq`) into a technology-mapped gate netlist, the tools strip away loop bounds, tile dimensions, and buffer-staging rules at the exact stages where logic restructuring, retiming, and placement expose physical wire delay and routing congestion. Once Boolean optimization and gate sizing flatten module boundaries, an architect or search tool can no longer map a critical-path violation or congestion hotspot in the routed layout cleanly back to the upstream loop schedule or scratchpad banking choice that caused it. To close the loop between physical signoff and architectural exploration, compiler and EDA builders need provenance graphs that survive logic optimization and physical synthesis without blocking the cross-boundary transformations that make the hardware efficient.

- **How can dynamic workload summaries stay predictive when compiler changes rewrite the executed instruction stream?** Classical trace summaries such as SimPoint basic block vectors ($w_{\text{BBV}}$) count dynamic execution against the static basic blocks of a fixed binary, so compiler transformations such as loop fusion, tiling, or vector register grouping ($LMUL$) invalidate those coordinates and shift cache-miss and memory-bank contention patterns. If a team has to re-profile full execution traces after every compiler schedule edit, joint hardware–software search becomes far too slow; if it reuses embeddings captured under an older schedule instead, the performance predictor is left blind to newly introduced memory stalls. Co-design tools need factorized workload representations that separate an algorithm's intrinsic data-reuse structure from schedule-dependent memory traffic, while signaling when a schedule change is large enough to require capturing a fresh trace.

## Summary

Useful architecture datasets are built around the engineering questions they must answer. Specifications, goals, block diagrams, workload descriptions, and design rationale establish what a study needs to know; public repositories and project archives supply some of that information. Missing observations require collection through tools or measurement. What a study can conclude depends on its access terms, acquisition budget, sampling distribution, and curation, including the failures and unresolved cases that successful runs alone would conceal.

Reusable knowledge explains when an observation should guide another decision. In the mapping study, an account of how local-memory reuse affects latency carries more meaning than an isolated winning tile size, while the live state determines whether that explanation applies now. A compact feature vector may suffice for prediction across fixed options; proposing a new schedule requires operations and dependencies that a compiler can transform. Linked representations let a design system consult existing information, acquire missing observations, and preserve the reasons behind its next action.

::: {.callout-takeaways}
- **Define the sample around the question, and budget for its coverage.** Identify the design, workload, software, observations, and conditions the task needs, and assess existing datasets against them before collecting. Count setup, compilation, checks, tool execution, licenses, and human effort; repetitions, new workload cases, and new designs resolve different uncertainties, so more rows do not automatically improve coverage.
- **Curate results without erasing their meaning.** Preserve units, versions, dependencies, and evaluation groups. Distinguish measured violations, censored bounds, and unresolved attempts so missing results do not become false training labels.
- **Keep architectural knowledge conditional.** Connect an explanation to the observations, assumptions, and counterexamples that support it. Check whether those conditions still apply when hardware, software, or workloads change.
- **Choose representations for what the method must do.** Predictors need features available when predictions are made. Generators and planning methods need expressible changes and a path back to artifacts that can be compiled, implemented, and checked. Linked views preserve relationships that one encoding may omit.
- **Plan for permitted use and reuse.** Access to source material does not establish permission for every training, retrieval, or sharing use. Preserve applicable restrictions through derived datasets and representations, and distinguish what others can reproduce from what requires restricted sources.
:::

With their representations and handoff records in place, our two Lighthouse studies now expose very different candidate spaces, data needs, and evaluation costs. Choosing how to act on those handoffs is the next decision (@sec-methods-generation-prediction-optimization), starting with whether direct tool evaluation is already sufficient or whether prediction, generation, optimization, or their combination can find a better design or reduce the total cost of reaching it.
